extracted.intended_audience: general readers; comedians and comedy scholars researching or performing the joke
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the conventional structure, themes, and performance considerations for telling the offensive, taboo-defying joke known as 'The Aristocrats.' Useful for performers and analysts who want to understand the joke's format and why it works (or fails).

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup
rubrics_metrics.description: A family act (or a representative, usually a head of household) goes in to see a talent agent about booking their act. The agent asks what their act consists of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the conventional opening that frames the narrative and prompts the elaborate description of the act; it establishes the agent/listener as the audience foil who will react to the act's outrageous content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act (performance/description)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the whole family is present, the act is performed for the agent; otherwise it is described, in as much detail as the teller prefers, typically ad lib. Traditionally, the description is tasteless and ribald, with the goal to significantly transgress social norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tellers may perform the act or narrate it; the level of detail and inventiveness is up to the teller. The act's descriptive richness and willingness to violate taboos are core to the joke's effect; restrained or sanitized descriptions undermine it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch line
rubrics_metrics.description: The shocked (or intrigued) agent asks what the act is called, and the proud answer (sometimes delivered with a flourish) is: 'The Aristocrats!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punch line relies on incongruity between the vulgar, transgressive act and the refined-sounding name. Timing and delivery (often a flourish) matter to land the incongruity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transgressive content / outrageousness as primary objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the objective of the joke is its transgressive content, it is most often told privately. When told to audiences who know the punch line, the joke's humor depends on the described outrageousness of the family act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joke's purpose is to push social norms; success hinges on how far and imaginatively the teller transgresses. This central objective explains why the joke is typically shared among comedians rather than broad public performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience familiarity and privacy considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When told to audiences who know the punch line, the joke's humor depends on the described outrageousness of the family act. Because the objective of the joke is its transgressive content, it is most often told privately, such as by comedians to other comedians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joke is usually meant for in-group settings; telling it publicly (especially to audiences unfamiliar with the format) risks misunderstanding, offense, or bombing. Tailor content and setting to the audience's expectations and tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvisation / ad lib freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: The act is typically described 'in as much detail as the teller prefers, typically ad lib.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tellers are expected to improvise and expand on the act creatively. The ad-libbed, personalized nature is part of the joke's tradition and allows comedians to showcase verbal inventiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of taboo themes (common content examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Taboo elements such as racism, animal cruelty, incest, rape, child sexual abuse, coprophilia, coprophagia, bestiality, necrophilia, cannibalism, and murder are common themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These themes are given as frequent building blocks for escalating the act's outrageousness. Their inclusion is characteristic of the joke but also explains its offensiveness and why it is generally confined to private/comic circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format flexibility / template nature
rubrics_metrics.description: This joke typically has these elements—alternative versions may change this form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Setup → Act → Punch line template is a flexible framework; individual tellings can vary widely in length, specific incidents invoked, and performance style while maintaining the core structure.
